nurseries.name: Guildford Garden Centre

touches.summary: Touch 1 goodwill intro. Flagged 612 products listed, linked their page, offered corrections and asked for their peak fruit tree season. No reply.
Re: treestock.com.au, and a quick visit?

Emma: first email got buried, apologised. Will look at the site properly. Happy to meet in person at the garden centre. Mondays before 2.30pm quietest; next week works. Peak bare root season, bagging a couple thousand trees.

In-person visit, about an hour with Emma at the garden centre. No pitch, nothing commercial. She knows who Benedict is now and likes the idea of the site. Flagged that our nursery page shows only seed packets in its top 20. Confirmed the delivery boundary on their site is accurate. Explained the bare root pre-order model. Offered a possible way to get their stock listings without scraping.

open_action.what: Reply to Emma thanking her for the hour, and take up her offer of a direct stock feed: ask what format they can export (CSV or XML) and how often it refreshes. Also tell her the top-20 on her nursery page is fixed, and that we carry her out-of-stock bare root lines with a notify-me on each, so her pre-registration list is not the only place a collector can wait. Do not ask for registration volumes. Dale to draft.

nurseries.notes:
WA, Perth metro delivery only; Emma confirmed 2026-08-17 that the boundary published on their site is accurate. In person visitable from Perth (Guildford, ~20 min from CBD). Contact is Emma. 859 products tracked, 225 in stock at 2026-08-17 (post DEC-301 filter). 127 clicks / 119 visitors in the 90d to 2026-08-13. Geo is unverifiable (DEC-270 free geo DB returns empty region/city), so do NOT describe those visitors as local. Touch 1 (2026-03-30) was buried, not ignored; Emma said so herself on 2026-08-13. Mondays before 2.30pm are quietest.

BARE ROOT MODEL (Emma, 2026-08-17 visit; corrected by Benedict same day). They order bare root stock in around June. It goes first to a pre-registration list, then anything uncollected after 2 weeks is released to the general public, and whatever still does not sell is potted up and sold on as potted stock. Most bare root is spoken for before the public ever gets a chance at it.

Crucially, those lines DO appear on their website, they just only ever show as out of stock. So we hold them: 161 bare root lines at 2026-08-17, 102 of them out of stock, including Cox's Orange Pippin, Angelina Burdett, Coe's Golden Drop, Nijisseiki and the Minnie Royal/Royal Crimson cherry multigrafts. This is a feature, not a gap. Our variety pages give a collector a second place to be notified from, independent of Guildford's own registration list, and that notification surface is the thing to upsell to nurseries later.

Do NOT ask Emma for registration volumes. They live in a spreadsheet with thousands of rows and she is not going to share them.

They deliberately do not import some deciduous stock that is too susceptible to pests, shot hole borer being the live Perth problem. It does not generally affect fruit trees, but it does affect much of the deciduous range they would otherwise bring in. Absence of a variety at Guildford is sometimes a policy decision, not a stock-out.

Stock levels are kept deliberately accurate: an online-vs-shop conflict causes real problems when the last plant sells twice. Treat Guildford availability data as high quality.

Emma may be able to supply stock listings directly instead of us scraping. Not yet specified as to format or cadence.
